source_refs.note: Exercise 13.2, Question 4: show that 2x dy/dx + y = 2 sqrt(x) for y = sqrt(x) - 1/sqrt(x) (book p.255).

blocks.explanation:
Yeh "show that" (saabit karo) wala sawal hai.
Humein pehle \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) nikalna hai, phir usay left side mein rakh kar dikhana hai ke right side ke barabar ban jata hai.
Plan: root ko powers mein likhna, differentiate, \(2x\) se guna, \(y\) jama, aur simplify.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sqrt{x} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} = x^{1/2} - x^{-1/2}\), \(x > 0\).
Saabit karna hai: \(2x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 2\sqrt{x}\).
Tareeqa: Power rule se \(\frac{dy}{dx}\), phir left side (LHS) ko simplify karte jayenge jab tak right side (RHS) na ban jaye. "Show that" mein hamesha ek side se shuru kar ke doosri tak pohanchte hain.

Differentiate karein
\[\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} + \frac{1}{2}x^{-3/2}\]
Kyun: \(x^{1/2}\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2}\). \(-x^{-1/2}\) ka derivative \(-(-\frac{1}{2})x^{-3/2} = +\frac{1}{2}x^{-3/2}\); do minus mil kar plus.
Dhyan dein: Yahan sign ki ghalti poora proof bigaar deti hai; minus guna minus plus hota hai.

\(y\) jama karein
\[2x\frac{dy}{dx} + y = x^{1/2} + x^{-1/2} + x^{1/2} - x^{-1/2}\]
\[= 2x^{1/2} = 2\sqrt{x}\]
Kyun: \(+x^{-1/2}\) aur \(-x^{-1/2}\) cancel ho gaye, aur do \(x^{1/2}\) mil kar \(2\sqrt{x}\) bane. Yahi RHS hai, to proof mukammal.

Tasdeeq
\[\text{At } x = 4:\ y = 2 - \frac{1}{2} = 1.5,\ y' = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{16}\]
\[8 \times \frac{5}{16} + 1.5 = 2.5 + 1.5 = 4 = 2\sqrt{4}\]
Kyun: Ek number rakh kar dekha, dono sides 4 aayin. Yeh proof nahi, magar is se yaqeen ho jata hai ke koi ghalti nahi hui.
